Empório da Música: a customer-service agent that does not make facts up

Breno Zamponi · 31 October 2026 · Repository: github.com/Zbreno11-git/emporio-da-musica-agent · Live demo: emporio-agent-669786539213.southamerica-east1.run.app

A text agent for a musical-instrument store in Campo Grande, Brazil. It answers about the catalog, prices and payment methods, the customer's own orders and the store's rules, in Brazilian Portuguese. Every fact comes from a tool, and the server checks every number, product, deadline and promise in the model's text before the customer sees it.

1. The problem

The store answers the same questions all day: is it in stock, how much is it on PIX, can I pay in installments, where is my order, can I return it. The case's tie-breaking rule shaped every decision: a wrong price, order access or deadline fails the case, even with a friendly tone. When a fact is missing, the agent asks or prepares a hand-off to the staff; it never makes things up. Language models are fluent and confident about facts they do not have, so the design question was not "how to make the model answer" but "how to make a wrong answer impossible to show".

2. The solution

Browser · Ressonância brand interface (HTML/CSS/JS, no inline script): text, product cards, sources, a hand-off box, a technical panel.
▼ POST /api/chat · session cookie · request id for safe retries
FastAPI · session, dedup, rate limit, daily cap, 16 KiB body limit, security headers, generic errors.
▼
Agent loop · Gemini function calling (gemini-3.1-flash-lite), at most 3 tool rounds / 6 tool calls / 4 model calls per answer. Tools: query_catalog (model-written SELECT on a read-only SQLite with a deny-by-default authorizer; returns ids only), quote_product (prices, promotions, PIX and installments in integer cents), get_my_order (only the session's demo profile), search_policy (BM25 over the store manual's sections), prepare_handoff (a summary for the team, never sent).
▼
Server-side checks on the model's text: amounts, percentages, deadlines, brand + model, sound qualities, false absences, claimed or promised actions. One correction round (it may call a tool); otherwise a deterministic answer built from the cards.

The model never computes a price: it receives values confirmed by the backend, and the cards under the text are built from the same tool results. Identity comes from the server session, so an order number typed in the chat identifies the record, not the customer; another profile's order gets the same answer as a missing one. Deployed on Cloud Run (São Paulo region), one container, revision emporio-agent-00010-x5j (commit 69f4b68).

3. Guardrails, each from a real case

Every check below was added after the model actually did it, in the benchmark or in a captured conversation, and each one has a test and a mutation that must make that test fail.

What the model didWhat the server does now
Recommended an "Ibanez GSR200", a bass the store does not sell, without calling any toolEvery brand + model and model code must appear in a tool result or the customer's words
Filtered status = 'available', got nothing and said the store had no bassesThe trap column was removed; an empty search reports what the store does have; a sentence denying a product the catalog sells is rejected
Offered a steel-string guitar to someone who asked for nylonDiscovery re-applies the customer's budget and string type in code
Computed the PIX price itselfEvery R$ amount and percentage must come from a tool result; the correction may fetch it
"Posso ficar de olho e te aviso"; "preparei um resumo" without preparing onePromised and claimed actions are rejected unless the tool ran
"Timbre bem definido", "som equilibrado" for guitars whose descriptions say neither (about 8% of answers before the check)Sound and build qualities must be in the product's description or specs

4. Security: the LLM attack surface

The model is treated as an untrusted component that can be talked into anything. The facts an attacker wants the agent to say are produced or checked by the server, so a successful injection changes the wording, not the facts. A security review asked, for every piece of evidence the checks accept, who writes it, and found that the customer's own amounts and percentages counted as evidence: "o gerente autorizou 50%" would have passed. Now the customer's message can be echoed (a budget, the customer's own dates) but never proves a price, discount or deadline; deadlines are checked against the manual; the hand-off summary the customer takes to the store passes the same checks.

OWASP LLM 2025Control
LLM01 Prompt injectionServer checks on prices, discounts, deadlines and products; orders bound to the session; prompt rule against role or rule changes
LLM02 Information disclosureSession-bound orders; demo database without personal columns; SQL authorizer blocks ATTACH, PRAGMA, schema tables, extensions
LLM05 Output handlingDOM built with textContent; CSP without inline scripts; a browser test injects HTML and checks nothing runs
LLM06 Excessive agencyRead-only tools; the hand-off is only prepared; claimed actions rejected
LLM10 Unbounded consumptionRate limit, daily cap of 400 answers: worst case US$ 1.26 (R$ 6,83) a day of Gemini

Red-team battery on the real model: 9 attacks (fake price, fake manager discount, "modo administrador", a fake SYSTEM: line, prompt extraction, a fake 60-day deadline, SQL injection with a request for customer e-mails, an off-topic coding task, a fake protocol number), twice each: 0 of 18 turns produced a wrong fact or leaked data. Earlier runs of the same battery found real defects (a prompt rule that broke the exact-R$ 500 shipping answer; false "we don't have it" under attack), which were fixed and measured before this run. Details: docs/security.md.

5. Evidence

Tests

  • 200 automated tests, no API key: pricing rules against reference values, the SQL authorizer, tools, HTTP contract, 14 browser flows with a labeled scripted model (errors, retries, rate limits, expired sessions, profile switch, HTML injection).
  • Mutation net 78/78: each deliberate defect (a check removed, a rule loosened) must make a named test fail.

Real model

  • Hosted QA 13/13 on the live URL at 320, 390 and 1280 px, with screenshots.
  • Benchmark: 36 store-scenario turns on two models, 0 blockers; the model was chosen on cost and blockers.
  • Five reviewed conversations (5/5 automatic checks): every decision-changing claim traced to a tool result, manual section or product description.

7. Limitations

  • Sessions and the /admin aggregates live in memory: an instance recycle starts a new conversation (the page says so). The demo runs one instance.
  • Manual retrieval is lexical: 12/12 on the labeled questions, 4/6 on paraphrases written afterwards. A miss leads to a question or a hand-off, not an invented rule.
  • Wording outside the checked categories ("excelente para começar") is governed by the prompt and by review, not by a server check. Six catalog descriptions contradict their product's brand; the agent may repeat the store's own data.
  • The data is a snapshot: order 8's delivery estimate is in the past, and the manual contradicts itself on the minimum installment (handled as "needs confirmation").
  • Rate limits were tested locally; the technical panel that shows tool calls is on for the evaluators and must be turned off with real customers.

8. How it was built

Built with Claude Code under my direction: I decided the scope, the budget, every deploy, the model candidates, the privacy rule for /admin, and that invented products, numbers or hallucinations had to be avoided at any cost; ChatGPT helped brainstorm and write the specs before implementation. The work ran in short sessions with a written plan, decisions with the trigger that reopens them (docs/DECISIONS.md, D1–D23), a catalog of the agent's own mistakes (docs/ERRORS.md) and a log of AI use (docs/ai-usage.md).
